+<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" ?>
+<class name="Trail2D" inherits="Node2D" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="../class.xsd">
+	<brief_description>
+		A 2D trail that can optionally be textured.
+	</brief_description>
+	<description>
+		This node spawns a 2D polyline trail behind it's position when transformed. [Trail2D] is not a mathematical polyline, i.e. the segments are not infinitely thin. It is intended for rendering and it can be colored and optionally textured.
body:
```suggestion
		This node spawns a 2D polyline trail behind it's position when transformed. [Trail2D] is not a mathematical polyline, i.e. the segments are not infinitely thin. It is intended for rendering. It can be colored and optionally textured. See also [Line2D] for drawing lines that have an infinite lifetime (such as ropes).
```

Also modify the `Line2D.xml` description to refer to Trail2D.

The default value makes lines that look a bit rough on sharp turns. It also requires a fair amount of motion from the node to actually start drawing a line (which can be especially noticeable in projects with a low viewport resolution, i.e. pixel art). I suggest a value that makes more detailed lines out of the box: ```suggestion float segment_length = 10.0f; ``` It'll be a bit slower to render for very long lines, but with the default lifetime of 1 second, I doubt the line has a lot of time to get complex. ### 30 ### 10

Well the Line2D gives the ability to set and edit the points manually and the line editing plugin and you wouldn't want that on the Trail2D, so I assumed I had to make it a separate node, but if it's possible to hide all that stuff I can move over to it inheiriting Line2D.
